carbon.$description: Carbon — Body text, structural hairlines, dark icon strokes — the universal ink that defines every other element on the page

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas, card surfaces, input fields, button text on dark fills

fog.$description: Fog — Body background wash, second surface tier below cards

silver.$description: Silver — Input borders, subtle dividers between content bands

mist.$description: Mist — Card borders — a half-step lighter than the structural hairline, used to separate stacked cards from the canvas

ash.$description: Ash — Muted icon strokes, inactive nav borders, secondary metadata

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Heavy icon borders, strong dividers, secondary structural lines that need more weight than #000 hairline

onyx.$description: Onyx — Deepest text tier for high-emphasis labels over light surfaces

graphite.$description: Graphite — Primary action button fill — the dark solid button (Sign in, Randomize); slightly lifted from pure black to read as a surface, not absence

cobalt-pulse.$description: Cobalt Pulse — Link text, icon dots, chromatic borders — the blue half of the system, used to mark tokens, active links, and the start of gradients

ultraviolet.$description: Ultraviolet — Outlined action border, secondary link accent — appears as a stroke on ghost controls and as the mid-stop in gradient transitions

spectrum-bridge.$description: Spectrum Bridge — Blue wash for highlight backgrounds, decorative bands, and soft emphasis behind content. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

aurora-wash.$description: Aurora Wash — Hero card gradient — soft translucent wash from ember through pink to cobalt, a 30% opacity field that sits behind the launch prompt

neuehaasunica.$description: All interface type — body, nav, buttons, cards, inputs, links, icons labels. Weight 400 for body and secondary; 500 for buttons and emphasized labels; 600 reserved for section headings. Tabular figures ('tnum', 'lnum') on all numeric displays so token counts and prices align in columns.

silka.$description: Supplementary display face — used sparingly for editorial moments and icon-adjacent labels where a different texture is needed from the interface default
